question: The rules under which vehicles are approved for the installation of tow bars without the need for additional inspection are laid down in Regulation (EU) 2018/858 (on the approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles and their trailers, and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles).

Some models (including a 2018 Fiat 500) cannot be approved for this, although similar models of a similar vintage (2016, 2017) can. The national authorities maintain that this is due to the manufacturer’s type-approval under the EU vehicle approval framework (Regulation (EU) 2018/858).

No objective or technical explanation can be given as to why the vehicle is excluded, including whether the difference stems from EU legislation or from the manufacturer’s choice at the time of type-approval. 1.

Can the Commission provide clarification as to whether Regulation (EU) 2018/858 contains requirements or restrictions that can explain why vehicles of the same model cannot be approved for tow bars depending on the year they were made, or whether such differences depend solely on the manufacturer’s choice at the time of typeapproval?

Does the Commission take the view that the current application of the EU’s typeapproval rules is transparent enough for consumers, including with regard to access to a clear technical and legal justification when national authorities refuse approval on the basis of the manufacturer’s type-approval?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.3.2026) The EU law1 provides that all motor vehicles must have a towing device fitted at the front. This allows for the removal of damaged or stranded vehicles from the road. The installation of towing devices in the rear of passenger cars2, on the other hand, depends on whether these cars are suitable for towing loads.

This is a choice of the manufacturer and needs to be declared by the vehicle manufacturer in the information document3 when applying for the approval of the respective vehicle type. Towing devices fitted to the vehicles shall be able to withstand a tractive and compressive static force equivalent to the force of gravity acting on at least half the technically permissible maximum laden mass of the vehicle.

Depending on their specific design and technical characteristics as well as approved wheel tyre combinations, different variants or versions of the same vehicle model and brand may differ as regards their suitability for towing loads.

The manufacturers must clearly specify in the vehicle technical handbook or user’s instructions the information on the towing capabilities of the vehicle and on the mechanical coupling devices installed.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02018R0858-20240701. 2 Vehicles of category M . 1 3 See point 2.11.5 of the information document referred to in Article 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858.
